Grok Build sessions get orbs. That is this release.

0.5.0 shipped the pairing work and deleted the Remote Control relay. Grok
Build support was already written and sitting on an open PR against `develop`
(#135); it did not make that tag. This one is that PR, nothing else.

Still a beta. What follows was measured against grok 1.0.13 on a real Mac;
Windows Grok has not been run. See *Known limitations*.

## New: Grok Build sessions as orbs

A live Grok session now shows up as an orb, labelled `cli:grok`, titled from
Grok's own `summary.json` — `generated_title`, and `/rename` when you have
used it. Click it and the chat panel is the real conversation, read off
`updates.jsonl` (ACP `session/update` envelopes), not a model's account of
it.

**This used to almost work, and that was the bug.** Grok's Claude Code
compatibility layer loads `~/.claude/settings.json`, so Claude Buddy's Claude
Code hook was already firing for Grok sessions. The status file said
`cli:claude`, and auto-color appended a Claude Code `agent-color` record into
Grok's own transcript. The hook now treats `GROK_SESSION_ID` /
`GROK_HOOK_EVENT` as the source of truth, even when argv still says `claude`,
and it never writes into Grok's `updates.jsonl`.

Grok has no `/color` — `/theme` is TUI-wide. Auto-color derives a ring from
the working directory into the status file and stops there.

`install-hooks.sh` wires Grok when it finds `~/.grok` or `grok` on PATH;
`install-grok-hooks.sh` is the per-CLI repair. Grok's `~/.grok/hooks/*.json`
is always trusted — there is no Codex-style review step.

## New: usage orbs for Grok (off by default)

Settings → **Grok Build** has the same four switches Claude Code and Codex
already had — show sessions, chat panel, reply, extra `GROK_HOME` accounts —
plus usage orbs.

A Grok usage orb wears the **weekly credit window** Grok already fetches.
There is no five-hour cap, so that ring is omitted rather than drawn at zero.
The figure is as fresh as the last Grok session on this machine: Claude Buddy
reads the `billing: fetched credits config` line out of
`$GROK_HOME/logs/unified.jsonl` and does not hold Grok's login token.

## Which file do I want

| Platform | Download |
| --- | --- |
| macOS, Apple silicon (M1 and later) | `ClaudeBuddy-0.5.1-beta-osx-arm64.dmg` |
| macOS, Intel | `ClaudeBuddy-0.5.1-beta-osx-x64.dmg` |
| Windows 10/11, 64-bit | `ClaudeBuddy-0.5.1-beta-win-x64-setup.exe` |

The `ClaudeBuddySpeech-0.5.1-beta-*.zip` assets are the optional high-quality
voice engine. **You do not download these yourself** — the app fetches the
right one when you turn the setting on. They are published here because that is
where it looks.

The .NET runtime is bundled; nothing else is needed. `SHA256SUMS.txt` covers
every file — verify with `shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS.txt` on macOS or
`Get-FileHash <file> -Algorithm SHA256` on Windows.

## Upgrading from 0.5.0-beta

**macOS**: replace the app in Applications. The signing identity is unchanged,
so Automation permission and click-to-focus carry over.

**Local Network permission does not.** Same CDHash rule as 0.5.0: replacing
the app loses the grant, and paired machines plus an OpenClaw gateway start
failing with `No route to host`. Approve it again in System Settings →
Privacy & Security → Local Network. A headless Mac still cannot; pair from
the machine with a screen and add the headless one by address.

**Windows**: run the new setup over the old one; it upgrades in place and
leaves your hook configuration alone.

Then run the hook installer so Grok is wired — `install-hooks.sh` inside the
app, or the **Install Hooks.command** on the DMG. Restart any open sessions,
Grok included. Hooks are read once at session start.

A Grok session that already had an orb labelled as Claude Code will correct
itself on the next hook fire after that restart.

## Installing fresh

**macOS** — open the DMG, drag Claude Buddy to Applications, then double-click
**Install Hooks.command**. Launch from Applications; nothing appears in the
Dock and no window opens, which is correct — look in the menu bar.

**Windows** — run the setup. Per-user, so no UAC prompt. Leave the hook
checkboxes ticked; tick **"Wire hooks for Claude Code running inside WSL"**
too if you use it.

### The hook step is not optional

Claude Buddy learns about your sessions from a hook that Claude Code, Codex,
and Grok each run. Until it's wired in, the app starts and runs correctly and
shows **nothing at all**. The installers offer to wire it up; let them.
Existing settings are backed up first, and re-running repairs rather than
duplicating.

## Known limitations

Everything below is named because it was not measured, not because it is
expected to fail.

- **Windows Grok, WSL Grok, and a second `GROK_HOME` account have not been
  run.** The PowerShell installer and hook path exist; CI runs the Windows
  hook tests; a real `grok` on Windows has not.
- **A real Grok permission-prompt pane has not been captured**, so dialog
  buttons in the chat panel are assumed rather than verified. PostToolUse is
  not wired until that is measured.
- **Whether `spawn_subagent` is a new `grok` pid** (team arrows) or
  in-process is unknown. An in-process spawn must not be hidden by the
  superseded-by-pid rule; that path is untested against a live spawn.
- **The exact JSON key `/rename` writes** when `title_is_manual` is true has
  not been seen. The hook prefers `title` in that case, then
  `generated_title`.
- **Usage orbs are as fresh as the last Grok session's log line.** There is
  no public `grok usage` CLI, and this app does not hold Grok's token, so
  there is no five-minute poll the way Claude Code usage orbs have.
- **Local Network consent is lost on every upgrade**, same as 0.5.0.
- **Windows installers are unsigned** — SmartScreen warns; choose **More info →
  Run anyway**. macOS builds are signed and notarized and open normally.

`docs/grok-findings.md` is the record of what was actually read off grok
1.0.13 versus assumed.
